MAJOR: `Authority` migration check compares `schema_migrations.version IN (16,18,19,20) HAVING count(*)=4`; if `version` is text (e.g. `'0018'`) or the table is absent, the query errors and every GET returns 503, making AC-2 unreachable. Confirm column type, and map "table missing" to `migration_missing` rather than `db_unavailable`.

AC-5 red→green E2E proof rests on `TestBacklogAuthorityWithDB` / `TestBacklogAuthorityFailsClosed`, which `t.Skip` unless `PF_RUNTIME_DSN` is set; default CI never executes the 200 path or the DB-outage 503 path. `engineering/trails/BI-PF-1509-red.txt` and `-rls-role.txt` cited in `ac_evidence` are not in this candidate.

`_db_for(scope)` ignores its argument: with `PF_BACKLOG_DB=on`, every scope (PF-SB and PF-GP) switches to DB-only save/delete and local item files are no longer written or removed — a storage-authority change beyond the declared non-goal "no PF-GP workflow changes", and outside `review_scope.files`.

Docs and code disagree on the DB-mode default (`docs/BACKLOG-DB-SSOT.md` and the `_backlog_db_mode` docstring say "on"; `config/env-flags.json` and the code default to "off") — operators will misread which store is authoritative.

`backlogAuthority` sets `edp_backlog_authority_startup_ok=0` on any 503 and never restores it on success, contradicting the runbook claim that "a single admin probe 503 is not paged" (the `startup_ok == 0 for 10m` rule is armed from the request path).

Index DDL on `backlog_items` (0018 `CREATE INDEX … INCLUDE (id)`) takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the SoR table during deploy and will abort under `lock_timeout=5s`; 0020 then drops and recreates the same index, doubling the DDL window on a hot table.

[OUT_OF_SCOPE] The candidate bundles a large framework/tooling change set (config/*.json, design/gate checkers, precheck, docs) outside `review_scope`; not assessed here, but it dilutes the full-candidate review and the item boundary.
MINOR: No non-DB test exercises the HTTP 503 path, and no unit/integration coverage exists for the `timeout` reason code, although the design's coverage and failure matrix claim it.
`test_backlog_migrations.py` only greps for `lock_timeout` and absence of `DELETE/TRUNCATE`; it never applies up/down, so trigger and counter behaviour is unproven.

Duplicate DB-mode detection: `core/backlog.py::_db_for`/`_backlog_db_mode` vs `core/id_allocator.py::_db_enabled`, plus `api/routers/backlog.py` reaching into the private `_db_enabled` — one owner is expected (reuse rule).
`reserve_ids` lets `reserve_shared`'s `RuntimeError` escape as a generic 500 instead of a structured envelope/503, diverging from the Go endpoints' failure contract.
`backlogReserve` maps generic DB errors to 503 without `Retry-After`, inconsistent with the authority endpoint's documented 503 + `Retry-After: 30`.
`tenant` query param is echoed into the JSON response and bound into `set_config` with no length/charset validation.
Error log emits `limits.Redact(err.Error())`; Postgres errors can carry statement/parameter text (tenant), so confirm redaction covers parameters, not only URLs.
NIT: `startup_ok` actually means "last authority check ok"; rename or add a separate gauge so request-path failures don't reuse the startup signal.
`HAVING count(*)=4` breaks if `schema_migrations` ever holds duplicate rows for a version; prefer an `EXISTS … WHERE version IN (…) GROUP BY` set check.
`ProductForgeBacklogAuthorityErrors` (`increase >= 3`) and `ProductForgeBacklogAuthorityErrorRate` (`rate > 0.05`) are near-duplicates; one alert is enough.
SUMMARY: Route, auth-before-method ordering, tenant guard, fixed 503 body, and fail-closed authority read are correctly implemented and covered by mux-level tests for AC-1/AC-3.
Largest risks: the migration-version predicate may make AC-2 permanently 503 depending on `schema_migrations` typing; the AC-2/AC-4 runtime proofs skip silently without `PF_RUNTIME_DSN`.
The DB-SSOT cutover bundled into `core/backlog.py`/`core/id_allocator.py` exceeds this item's declared scope/non-goals and its default-on documentation contradicts the code.
Observability semantics (startup gauge mutated by request failures) and the SoR index DDL need tightening before production rollout.
